jobs.title: Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRAVERSAL

Traversal https://www.traversal.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com is the AI Site Reliability Engineer (AI SRE) for the enterprise.

Production complexity was already outpacing what engineering teams could manage manually, and AI-generated code is accelerating that gap. Traversal is built for that challenge, autonomously understanding and reasoning across even the largest, most complex production environments to diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents. Our mission is to free engineers from endless firefighting and give them more time to focus on creative, high-impact work.

Today, Traversal operates in mission-critical environments at some of the world’s largest enterprises. Our roots remain deeply embedded in AI research, and we’ve brought together researchers from institutions including MIT, Harvard, Berkeley, Columbia, and Cornell with world-class technical staff and operators from companies like Google, Meta, Datadog, ServiceNow, and Citadel Securities to take on one of the hardest problems for AI to solve. Traversal is backed by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Hanabi, NFDG, and American Express Ventures.




THE ROLE

As a Strategy & Operations hire reporting to the Strategy & Operations Lead, you'll partner on Traversal's highest-priority cross-functional initiatives - from pricing and packaging to getting complex deals across the finish line to making sure we're executing against our annual operating plan. This is a generalist seat, not a narrow lane: you'll be handed ambiguous, high-stakes problems, expected to scope them, build the analysis, and drive them to execution end-to-end.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own cross-functional strategic projects end-to-end - scoping, analysis, and implementation - partnering with Sales, Product, Finance, and Engineering as needed.

 - Help get complex deals to the finish line - supporting structuring, internal approvals, and cross-functional coordination to clear blockers.

 - Own key parts of the annual operating plan process: track progress against goals, flag risks early, and help leadership course-correct.

 - Build financial and operational models to support decision-making across the business.

 - Build scalable, AI-native systems to streamline workflows and distribute insights across the business.

 - Act as a thought partner to executives on ambiguous, high-stakes problems - bring structure and a point of view, not just analysis.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 4-6 years of experience, ideally 2-3 years in management consulting, investment banking, or private equity, followed by 1-2 years in an operating role at an early-stage startup.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous, cross-functional projects end-to-end with minimal oversight.

 - Strong quantitative and analytical skills; comfortable building structured frameworks from scratch.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication - able to synthesize complex problems into clear recommendations for executives.

 - High ownership mentality - bias toward action, comfortable operating with limited process or precedent.

 - Generalist mindset: excited to work across pricing, deals, planning, and whatever the business needs next, rather than staying in one functional lane.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Financial fluency and experience building models (FP&A, LTV / CAC, pricing models, revenue build, unit economics).

 - Comfort leveraging AI tools to move faster and raise the quality of output (not slop).

 - Prior experience in a deal desk, pricing, or GTM strategy function.


COMPENSATION

We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance, and additional benefits.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time, in-person role in New York is $175,000–$250,000, plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are based on location, level, and role. Individual compensation is determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN US

Traversal is a place to take on hard, meaningful problems with real ownership from day one. You'll work alongside people who challenge you to grow, learn constantly, and help define a new category of infrastructure software. We think long term, move quickly, and hold a high bar without taking ourselves too seriously.

We offer competitive salary and equity packages, health insurance, fertility benefits, a great tech setup stipend and flexible time off. Plus lunch & dinner, in-office snacks, team happy hours and outings, an annual company offsite, and plenty of built in time to collaborate across teams.

Traversal is fully in-office, 5 days a week, based in New York near Madison Square Park. We have a collaborative, hard-working culture and are energized by building the future of AI-powered software maintenance.

THE ROLE

As a Field Marketing Manager you will  help build and execute programs that create and nurture meaningful relationships with enterprise technology leaders and drive pipeline growth.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of marketing, events, sales, and operations. You'll own the execution of executive experiences, industry conferences, regional events, partner activations, and relative integrated field marketing campaigns.

As an early member of a growing marketing team, you'll have the opportunity to help shape how we engage with and build our community through impactful and memorable moments.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own Traversal’s events and field marketing strategy across corporate events, sponsored trade shows, roadshows, workshops, and regional programs

 - Plan and execute world-class events from concept through completion, including timelines, budgets, vendors, logistics, and on-site execution

 - Develop and run regional field marketing initiatives aligned with pipeline acceleration goals.

 - Partner closely with sales

 - Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales and Marketing to plan initiatives aligned to brand and business goals.

 - Measure, analyze, and report on the performance of each initiative, including pipeline impact and ROI.

 - Continuously test, iterate, and improve programs based on performance data and field feedback.


REQUIREMENTS

 - 3–5 years of experience in B2B field marketing at a high-growth technology company.

 - Proven experience planning and executing executive events, customer programs, and field marketing initiatives.

 - Experience managing industry conferences, trade shows, and sponsorship activations from planning through post-event reporting.

 - Experience executing events for both highly technical audiences (engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, SRE, platform teams) and executive decision makers.

 - Experience measuring pipeline influence, campaign attribution, and event ROI.

 - Experience managing external vendors, agencies, and production partners.

 - Outstanding project management and organizational skills, paired with a keen attention to detail.

 - Experience partnering closely with Sales and GTM organizations to build integrated field marketing programs that support pipeline generation.

 - Comfortable working cross-functionally in a fast-paced startup environment where priorities evolve quickly.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business or a related field preferred

 - Willingness to travel approximately 30–50% as programs require.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Industry experience in AI, infrastructure, developer tools, cloud, observability, cybersecurity, or enterprise software.

 - Familiarity with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, or similar CRM and marketing automation platforms.

 - Basic design skills with the ability to create/edit marketing assets using Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or similar creative software.

 - Experience writing marketing and sales content that support events—including campaign emails, event invitations, landing pages, social media content, sales enablement materials, and other customer-facing communications.

THE ROLE

As our HR Business Partner, you'll shape how our team is supported, developed, and set up to do its best work as we grow. This role is ideal for someone who can advise leaders on big people decisions in the morning and fix a broken onboarding workflow in the afternoon, and who cares about getting both right.

You'll partner with our founders and leaders on org health, performance, and people strategy. You'll also own the full employee lifecycle, from onboarding through offboarding, handle employee relations, and lead core programs like performance reviews and compensation cycles. You'll work closely with leadership, Finance, Legal, and Recruiting, and you'll have a lot of room to build and automate the systems that support our people as we scale.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Strategic People Partner: Be a trusted advisor to leaders on org health, performance, team dynamics, and manager effectiveness. Turn business priorities into clear people recommendations and action plans.

 - Employee Relations & Performance: Own ER and performance cases end-to-end. That includes investigating issues, coaching managers through documentation, and guiding decisions in line with company policy and employment law.

 - Core People Programs: Lead and improve the programs that keep the company running: performance reviews, talent reviews, engagement, compensation cycles, and manager enablement.

 - Onboarding & First 90 Days: Own the new hire experience from pre-boarding through the 90-day mark. That covers paperwork and I-9s, account setup, day-one orientation, check-ins, and a buddy program. Remote and in-office hires should get an equally strong start.

 - Employee Lifecycle: Run internal transfers, promotions, terminations, and offboarding. Hold exit interviews and bring the themes back to leadership to improve retention and reduce risk.

 - Front Line for Questions: Be the first stop for employee and manager questions. Resolve what you can, route what you can't, and make sure nothing sits unanswered.

 - Policy & Compliance: Write and update HR policies, handbooks, and processes. Keep the company compliant with federal, state, and local employment law as we grow.

 - Data-Driven Insight: Use HRIS data to spot patterns, recurring pain points, and talent risks, then recommend practical fixes to leaders.

 - Build & Automate: Don't just run the process, build it. Write SOPs other people can actually use, and use AI and automation to take repetitive work (status chasing, packet assembly, case intake) off the team's plate.

 - Cross-Functional Partner: Work closely with Legal, Finance/Payroll, IT, Recruiting, and Workplace so handoffs are seamless.


REQUIREMENTS

 - 5–8 years in HR at a high-growth company, with a mix of HRBP/generalist and people operations work.

 - Broad HR Expertise: Hands-on depth in employee relations, performance management, onboarding and offboarding, and compensation cycles. You've handled sensitive situations on your own.

 - Employment Law Fluency: Working knowledge of federal, state, and local employment law, including I-9 and eligibility verification. You know when to flag something to Legal.

 - Strategic and Hands-On: You can advise a founder on org design in the morning and fix a broken onboarding workflow in the afternoon. No task is beneath you.

 - Systems & AI Savvy: Comfortable with HRIS and ticketing tools. You reach for AI and automation by instinct to create leverage.

 - Clear Communicator: You write clear, professional documentation with minimal review, build trust quickly, and push back thoughtfully when it matters.

 - Builder Mindset: You're at your best in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, and your processes are written down, current, and usable by someone else.
